title: POETS: Uncertainty-Aware LLM Optimization via Compute-Efficient Policy Ensembles
claim: Prior methods chain a reward ensemble and a separate single policy; ours collapses both into one policy ensemble interacting with the environment.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, cyclic loop arrows, left prior with three stacked boxes versus right ours with two
description: Two side-by-side cyclic diagrams made of rounded grey boxes joined by curved block arrows. The left panel (previous methods) stacks three boxes vertically: Single Policy at the top, Reward Ensemble in the middle (drawn as a layered stack to show multiple members), and Environment at the bottom. Two curved arrows loop on the left side, linking Environment to Reward Ensemble and Reward Ensemble to Single Policy. A large arrow on the right returns from Single Policy down to Environment. The right panel (ours) is simpler: a layered Policy Ensemble box on top and an Environment box below, joined by a single clockwise loop of two curved arrows. The palette is monochrome grey with dark navy outlines. The eye goes first to the larger, more complex left loop, then to the simpler right loop.
caption: Previous methods for sample efficient RL fit an uncertainty-aware reward model and separately train a single policy to trade off exploration and exploitation (left). POETS directly estimates reward uncertainty with policy ensembles (right).
abstract: Balancing exploration with exploitation is a core challenge in black-box optimization and reinforcement learning. We introduce POETS ($\textbf{Po}$licy $\textbf{E}$nsembles for $\textbf{T}$hompson $\textbf{S}$ampling), a novel framework that bridges uncertainty quantification and policy optimization. Our approach is grounded in the insight that policies trained with Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization implicitly encode an underlying reward function. Building on this, POETS bypasses the complex, nested process of training an uncertainty-aware reward model and separately fitting a policy to this model. Instead, we directly train a policy ensemble to capture epistemic uncertainty by matching implicitly encoded reward functions to online, bootstrapped data. To overcome the prohibitive compute and memory constraints of ensembling Large Language Models (LLMs), POETS utilizes an efficient architecture: the ensemble shares a pre-trained backbone while maintaining diversity through independent Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) branches. Theoretically, we show that POETS implicitly approximates KL-regularized Thompson sampling, a principled optimization strategy with optimal cumulative regret bounds of $O(\sqrt{T Î³_T})$. Empirically, we demonstrate that POETS achieves state-of-the-art sample efficiency across diverse scientific discovery domains, including protein search, therapeutic molecular design, and quantum circuit design. POETS also improves the optimization trajectory and out-of-distribution transfer of reinforcement learning across mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks, proving particularly robust in off-policy settings with experience replay or in small dataset regimes.
